headline: High: shared filesystem and overlapping write/network surfaces create medium-to-high risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between Mentat and TREK.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat shares state via filesystem and writes files; TREK uses MCP and real-time collaborative inputs. That creates a plausible bridge where TREK content can be written into files Mentat reads as trusted instructions, or vice versa. The interaction is documented only indirectly, so I choose medium rather than low because the shared filesystem is explicit and both agents can ingest external content.
conditions: IF TREK writes attacker-controlled text into a shared file that Mentat later reads
IF Mentat parses file contents as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent
Disable automatic instruction-following from file contents
Add provenance tags to shared artifacts
Review shared-file handoff before execution
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization at the orchestrator boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys; TREK touches reservations, documents, photos, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets. If they share files or workspace, sensitive TREK data can flow into Mentat and then out to a third-party model provider. The blast radius includes secrets and personal data, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or uploaded files
IF Mentat sends file contents from that workspace to its model provider
mitigations: Use separate storage volumes
Exclude secrets and reservations from shared folders
Redact sensitive fields before Mentat reads files
Rotate any exposed API keys or MFA secrets
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, while TREK has shared files and real-time collaborative state. Even without explicit git in TREK, overlapping writes to shared files can clobber edits or corrupt collaborative data. Because the conflict surface is explicit but not a full same-dir git lock scenario, medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or repository
IF TREK persists collaborative updates while Mentat applies diffs to the same files
mitigations: Assign disjoint write paths
Serialize edits through one orchestrator
Take a filesystem snapshot before concurrent runs
Pause one agent during the other's write phase
requires-engineering: add file-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and TREK is a collaborative planner with AI built in that can consume documents and act on travel data. If TREK treats Mentat's outputs as authoritative, a bad edit proposal can cascade into incorrect plans or stored records. The pathway is plausible in default collaborative workflows, but direct downstream action authority is not fully evidenced.
conditions: IF TREK ingests Mentat-generated diffs or text without verification
IF TREK applies those outputs to reservations, budgets, or documents
mitigations: Require human review before applying outputs
Cross-check outputs against source data
Limit Mentat output to suggestions only
Log provenance for imported content
requires-engineering: add validation rules before writeback

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles sensitive travel data, including documents, photos, email addresses, API keys, and MFA secrets, while Mentat handles source code and model-provider API keys. If travel PII or secrets are moved into Mentat's broader networked workflow, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify jurisdictions, so I avoid high and choose medium on policy-mismatch risk.
conditions: IF regulated travel documents or personal data are shared from TREK into Mentat
IF Mentat's provider retention differs from TREK's local storage policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Mentat inputs
Review retention settings for both systems
Document data-flow boundaries
Purge temporary files after use
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
